text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BANERJ AUCTION SEEN IN MARCH
Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj is likely to be privatized in March next year, following the cancelation of two privatization auctions in December.
-- BANKS HAVE HIGHER PROFITS
Brazil's large banks will end 1996 with the best results since the introduction of the anti-inflation Real Plan in 1994.
-- TAX ON OVERSEAS CASH REMITTANCES CANCELED
A new corporate tax law has reduced a 15 percent tax on movements of cash overseas to zero.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- IMPORTS OF SUPERFLUOUS GOODS REACH $1 BLN
Brazil has spent more than $1 billion on imported goods considered superfluous, which helps to explain the trade deficit estimated at $5 billion for 1996.
-- GOVT GETS HIGHEST APPROVAL RATING SINCE TAKING OFFICE
A poll shows the government has achieved its highest approval rating since taking office, with 47 percent of those interviewed saying the administration was good.
-- GOVT USES 100 MLN REAIS A MONTH FOR SECRET MEASURES
The federal government has spent 100 million reais a month on what are considered secret operations in the first two years of the Fernando Henrique Cardoso administration.
O GLOBO
-- LANDLESS MOVEMENT EYES CVRD LANDS IN 1997

The leader of the landless peasant movement says lands owned by state mining company CVRD in the northeast of Brazil and properties in the area of the Sao Francisco river would be the main targets for occupation and squatting in 1997.
-- LOW INFLATION HIDES INCREASES OF OVER 50 PCT
Although annual inflation has fallen to one digit this year, the prices of some goods have risen more than 50 percent.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
